title: The Producer of Kala Hiran Just Tore Up Salman Khan's Legal Notice on Camera. Then He Mentioned D-Company.
excerpt: Amit Jani claims he received death threats from the underworld over a film about the blackbuck poaching case. Salman's team wants it shut down. The teaser is still scheduled for June 20.
body:
The dispute between Salman Khan and the makers of *Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy* has escalated from legal posturing to something far more volatile. On Wednesday, producer Amit Jani posted a video to his Facebook page in which he held up a legal notice sent by Salman Khan's team — and tore it apart on camera.

Then he said the quiet part out loud: he claimed he had received death threats from D-Company, the criminal syndicate historically linked to Dawood Ibrahim.

## What the Film Is About

*Kala Hiran* is built around the blackbuck poaching case that has followed Salman Khan for nearly three decades. In 1998, during the shooting of *Hum Saath Saath Hain* in Jodhpur, Salman was accused of killing two blackbucks — an endangered species sacred to the Bishnoi community. The case has wound its way through Indian courts ever since. A trial court convicted him in 2018 and sentenced him to five years. A sessions court granted bail the same year. The matter is still pending in the Rajasthan High Court.

The film's poster, released in late May, showed a man holding a firearm and wearing a turquoise bracelet — an accessory widely associated with Salman Khan's public persona. Jani and director Bharat S. Shrinate announced the teaser would drop on June 20.

## Salman's Legal Response

Salman Khan's team, through the law firm DSK Legal, fired back with a legal notice to the film's casting director, Akshay Pandey. The notice demanded an immediate halt to all production and promotion. The argument: the film constitutes a "gross violation of personality rights," could damage Salman's reputation, and might interfere with ongoing judicial proceedings.

Salman's team emphasized that no permission had been given for the use of his name, likeness, or any incidents associated with him.

## The Producer's Defiance

Jani was not deterred. In his video response, he called the legal notice an act of intimidation by a celebrity exploiting his industry power. He quoted the late Urdu poet Rahat Indori to suggest a pattern of threats directed at those who question powerful figures.

"Our entire film is not a biopic of Salman Khan," Jani told ABP News. "It presents what is already available in the public domain and highlights the beliefs and history of the Bishnoi community." He said Salman Khan is "just a part" of the larger narrative.

Then came the D-Company reference. Without naming specific individuals beyond the syndicate, Jani claimed his team had received threats intended to force the film's cancellation. "We will handle D-Company from here," he said.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

The case sits at the intersection of two legal frontiers that matter far beyond Bollywood gossip.

The first is **personality rights** — an area of Indian law still being defined. Courts have increasingly recognized that public figures retain control over how their identity is used commercially and narratively. Earlier this week, the Delhi High Court granted Varun Dhawan protection against unauthorized AI deepfakes and commercial exploitation of his likeness. The Kala Hiran dispute pushes this boundary further: at what point does a real criminal case — one that played out in public courts and involved a protected species — become too personal to dramatize?

The second is **creative freedom**. Jani is not the first filmmaker to argue that events in the public record are legitimate subjects for cinema. But Salman Khan's legal team counters that even fictionalized portrayals, if clearly identifiable, can harm reputation and prejudice ongoing legal proceedings.

For NRIs who follow both Bollywood and the broader legal evolution of India's entertainment industry, this is a test case. The outcome could set the terms for which real-life stories Indian filmmakers are allowed to tell — and which powerful individuals can effectively veto.

## What Happens Next

The teaser launch, scheduled for June 20, now hangs in uncertain territory. No court hearing has been announced. Salman Khan's team has remained silent beyond the legal notice. Jani and his team show no sign of backing down.

The film does not yet have a confirmed release date. But the fight over whether it should exist at all may end up being more consequential than anything on screen.
